6.166.m:
A man, having bathed at that holy ford, should present a bull to a brāhmaṇa; / passing beyond all worlds, he goes to the supreme state.

Then, O Great Goddess, one should go to the daughter of the mountain, the Vārtraghnī,
where Śakra attained union with that virtuous woman.

Men of restrained mind who bathe there, / one who bathes obtains the fruit of ten horse sacrifices.

Whoever performs a śrāddha there, offering balls of sesame powder, / that man purifies his lineages, seven earlier and seven later.

Having bathed properly at the confluence and having worshipped the lord of the gaṇas, / he is not overcome by obstacles, nor is he abandoned by fortune.

Pārvatī said: / At the commencement of what work did Puraṃdara arrive / from heaven to this mortal world? You ought to tell me this.

And by what etymology is the river Vārtraghnī called so? / Tell me of that confluence, O god, which continually honors / Puraṃdara's city resounding with the chant of the Veda.

Mahādeva said: / In this very mortal world, this question arose formerly / from the great, righteous king renowned as Yudhiṣṭhira.
He asked Bhīṣma, the righteous one, who was knowledge personified. / What was spoken by him, O goddess, I shall explain before you.
For ten thousand years and ten hundred years, / a hair-raising battle took place between Vṛtra and Vāsava.
Then Śakra, having been defeated, made an agreement with Vṛtra / of non-hostility, abandoned his refuge, and went to my refuge.
At the holy confluence of the Vārtraghnī he gratified Śaṅkara. / Then, O goddess, I granted him a vision in the sky.
And the ashes that fell from my body on the bank of the earth, / a holy liṅga made by the gods was formed there, [named] Bhasmagātra, O goddess.
The Bhasmagātra Bhūteśvara [liṅga] was consecrated by Brahmā. / Merely by its sight, the murder of a brāhmaṇa dissolves away.
One is freed from all sins after performing a śrāddha on yuga-beginnings. / Then I became very pleased with the great-souled Indra:
“Whatever you desire, O god, all that indeed I give to you. / By means of this thunderbolt-union, you will swiftly slay Vṛtra.”
Śakra said: / “O Lord, by your favor I will slay with the thunderbolt / that unassailable son of Diti while you watch, O best of gods.”
Having spoken thus, Indra then set out toward the asura. / Then kettledrums sounded, especially in the army of the gods,
and mṛdaṅgas, ḍiṇḍimas, bherīs, and tūryas in great numbers; / and among all the asuras there arose a great craving for food.
And Maghavan became mighty in an instant. / Knowing him to be possessed [by divine power], the sages and the serpents
praised Śakra, the ruler, with praise and with cries of “Victory, victory!” / As that Śakra went into the presence, desiring battle, / being praised by the sages, his form became difficult to bear.
Mahādeva said: / Listen to me, O goddess, about the signs that suddenly appeared on Vṛtra's body / then at the forefront of the battle:
his mouth burned, becoming terrible, and extreme pallor came upon him; / there was a tremendous trembling of his limbs, and a burning breath arose;
his hair stood on end intensely, and his breathing became heavy; / a most dreadful meteor fell down, and others fell beside him;
vultures, crows, falcons, and cranes uttered dreadful cries; / they all circled above Vṛtra like a wheel.
Then Indra, mounting his elephant, arrived there. / Hand raised with the thunderbolt, Śakra there approached that daitya.
Then the lord of gods released an unearthly roar; / Śakra hurled his thunderbolt at Vṛtrāsura as he was exerting himself.
That thunderbolt, possessed of immense splendor, great like the fire of destruction, / was hurled; Śakra struck down the daitya Vṛtra on the shore of the ocean.
Then a roar arose once more from every side, / seeing Vṛtra slain, who had terrified all the gods.
A great shower of flowers fell upon Indra's head. / Having slain Vṛtra, the terrifying lord of dānavas,
the lord, being praised along with the immortals, entered the city of the gods. / Then, from the body of Vṛtra, a supreme splendor emerged:
the murder of a brāhmaṇa, most dreadful, frightening to the fierce world, / with a hideous face, deformed, black and tawny,
wearing a garland of skulls, emaciated, O daughter of the mountain, / smeared with blood, most wicked, smelling of fish, terrifying.
Having emerged, O Great Goddess, with such a terrifying form, / she then searched for Indra, O best of goddesses.
Then, rushing out and seeing the mighty Śakra, / she seized the king of the gods by the neck and clung tightly [to him].
And bewildered in the terror caused by the murder of a brāhmaṇa, / he hid within a lotus stalk, where he remained for many years.
Seized by her, O goddess, he became motionless. / And Śakra made every effort to remove her;
yet he was unable, O Great Goddess, to remove the murder of a brāhmaṇa. / The king of the gods, assuming a dreadful appearance as soon as seized by her,
approached the Grandfather and bowed with his head. / Knowing that Śakra had been seized by the murder of a foremost twice-born,
Brahmā reflected then, O best among goddesses. / While he was reflecting, she approached Brahmā and spoke these words:
“I have come into your presence, O lord, O god, who bestow honor; / what ought to be done by me, O god, you should declare.”
The Grandfather then spoke to that murder of a brāhmaṇa, O fortunate one, / with a sweet voice, briefly and truthfully:
“Let this king of gods be released; do what pleases me, O lady. / Tell me, what may I do for you today? What wish do you desire here?”
The Brahmin-slaughter [personified] said: / 'I shall depart from Śakra at your word, O best of men! / O god of gods, salutations to you; grant me an abode.'
Mahādeva said: / Having agreed to her with 'So be it', the grandfather [Brahmā] / then [devised] a means for Śakra to remove the Brahmin-slaughter.
Then, summoning the fire, Brahmā addressed these words: / 'O Jātavedas, take a fourth portion of the slaughter of Śakra!'
Agni said: / 'O Lord, what will be the cause of my release from the Brahmin-slaughter? / I wish to know this in truth, O you who are worshipped by the worlds.'
Brahmā said: / 'Whenever a man, having approached you as you blaze, will not offer into you / seeds, medicinal herbs, and sesame seeds first, or fruits, roots, firewood, and kuśa grass,
at that very moment [the Brahmin-slaughter] will leave you and will reside right there in him, / O carrier of oblations! Let the fever of your mind depart!'
Then the consumer of offerings to gods and ancestors accepted that word. / And the blessed grandfather thus attained what he desired.
Then the grandfather, having summoned the trees, herbs, and grasses, / began to speak of this matter, O fortunate one.
Then the trees, herbs, and grasses spoke exactly in the same way, as it was; / distressed like the fire, O goddess, they said to Brahmā:
'Speaking to us of the Brahmin-slaughter, O grandfather— / it is inherently placed [upon us], so you ought not to strike [us] again.
We perpetually endure fire, cold, / and rain driven by the wind, O god, as well as cutting and breaking.'
Brahmā said: / 'The man who, out of great delusion, causes / cutting and breaking of you without reason—she will go to him.'
Mahādeva said: / Then the great medicinal herbs and grasses, the great-souled ones, said, 'Om.' / Having honoured Brahmā, they departed just as they had come.
Then the god, the grandfather of the worlds, having summoned the apsarases, / spoke in sweet words, consoling them, O most virtuous one:
'This Brahmin-slaughter was incurred from Vṛtra, O excellent women; / accept the fourth part of it, as spoken by me.'
The apsarases said: / 'Having resolved to accept it at your command, O lord of gods, / the occasion of our release must be considered by you, O grandfather.'
The grandfather said: / 'He who engages in sexual union with menstruating women— / to him she will swiftly go. Let the fever of your mind depart!'
Mahādeva said: / Glad at heart when thus addressed, the hosts of apsarases, saying 'So be it', / returned to their own abodes and rejoiced then, O daughter of the mountain.
Then the god who creates the worlds, the grandfather, once more / thought of the waters, and thereupon they assembled.
Having all arrived and prostrated before Brahmā of immeasurable splendour, / the grandfather, they spoke this word, O goddess:
'Here we have arrived, O god, into your presence, O subduer of foes! / By your command, O lord of gods, give us your instruction, O master!'
Brahmā said: / 'This terrible Brahmin-slaughter has approached Puruhūta [Indra] from Vṛtra; / take a fourth portion of it!'
The waters said: / 'Let it be so, O lord of the world, as you tell us, O master! / But you ought to devise the time of our release.'
"You, O Indra of gods, are indeed the highest refuge of the entire world. / For what other favor could rescue us from distress?"
Brahmā said: / "Having thus made small his intellect, whichever man is bewildered in understanding,

And discharges phlegm, urine, or feces into you, / it is to him alone that it shall quickly go, and there indeed shall it reside. / From that will be your liberation; this is the truth I speak to you."
Mahādeva said: / "Then, having released the king of gods, O goddess of the gods, the killing of a brahmin / departed, and the lord of gods became exceedingly pleased by the command of the god.
Thus in a former cosmic age Indra incurred the killing of a brahmin. / Performing austerities at this sacred ford, purified in soul, he went to heaven.
Having then performed the horse sacrifice, he became freed from sin. / This is the Vārtraghnī at the Sābhramatī sacred ford, O daughter of the mountain."

6.169.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-eighth chapter, titled 'Glorification of the Vārtraghnī,' in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

Whichever man bathes there is certainly an inheritor of liberation, there is no doubt. / One should perform a śrāddha there for the sake of the liberation of the ancestors; / liberated together with them, he goes to the great world that grants happiness."

The one hundred seventieth chapter. Mahādeva said: / "Beyond that sacred ford there is a sacred ford known as Saṅgama, so it is heard. / Here the Sābhramatī Gaṅgā joined with the ocean.

Bathing and gifting should be performed there according to the rules, / where having bathed, even those who committed mortal sins are freed.

There a śrāddha should be performed by one desiring the welfare of one's own kin; / indeed, when a śrāddha is performed there, one surely dwells in the realm of the ancestors.

Where indeed the divine ocean constantly meets with the Gaṅgā, / even a killer of a brahmin is freed there; what to say of other sins?

Where dim-witted people do not recognize the sacred ford, / then indeed an excellent sacred ford should be established in my name."

6.171.m: Mahādeva said: / "Near the confluence is a true sacred ford celebrated in the worlds / called Āditya; higher than it there has been none, nor will there be.
One should indeed behold it, and bathe with a lotus, / and also worship with arka flowers and then with oleander flowers.
There people should always perform śrāddha and give gifts; / this Ādityaka sacred ford is pure and sin-destroying.
From its mere sight, the sacred ford grants merit even to those guilty of mortal sins."

6.172.m: Mahādeva said: / "Beyond that sacred ford there is a sacred ford renowned as Nīlakaṇṭha; / one desiring liberation should certainly always visit it.
With bilva leaves, incense, or lamps, O goddess of the gods, / a mortal obtains his desire from the sight of Nīlakaṇṭha.
Devoted to fasting, O goddess, he always abides in a solitary place; / whatever those people desire, he grants each of those things to them.
In the Kali age, O great goddess, it is indeed renowned as Kāśyapī."

6.173.m: Mahādeva said: / "Where the river Sābhramatī meets with Durgā, O goddess, / there is the confluence with the ocean; one should bathe there.
In the Kali age they will become free from fault, there is no doubt here. / There a śrāddha should be performed, at the confluence with Durgā.
Having gone there, especially the feeding of brahmins / and the gift of cows and female buffaloes should be performed according to the rules.
This [river] is fortunate, most fortunate, pure, sin-destroying, / on seeing which even a man is freed from sins, O goddess.
Just as the Gaṅgā is, so should this river Sābhramatī be known; / in the Kali age especially, O goddess, it grants fruits for a long time.
Even if there were a hundred tongues in my mouth, / even then I could never express all of her virtues."

6.174.m: Mahādeva said: / "Listen, O goddess, I shall proclaim a vow difficult to obtain in the three worlds, / hearing which a person is released from sins such as the killing of a brahmin.
For the sake of happiness of his devotees, the birth of the self-luminous one, / or a lunar day, a month, came into being as a maker of merit,
Reciting whose name, O goddess, one obtains eternal liberation; / he alone is the supreme self and the cause of all causes,

The soul of the universe, multiform, the blessed Lord, master of all, / by whom, the great-souled Nṛsiṃha, twelve suns were held; / he manifested himself out of a desire for the peace of his devotees."
Speak of the supreme abode called Nṛsiṃha, O sovereign Lord of the universe, / by the mere knowledge of which one may attain the world of happiness."
Mahādeva said: / "Having slain Hiraṇyakaśipu, to the god of gods, the teacher of the universe, / seated comfortably, situated upon his lap, [Prahrāda] spoke words—
Prahlāda, the best of the wise, [approached] the supreme slayer of his father.

Prahlāda said:
Obeisance to you, O Lord Viṣṇu, who possess the wondrous form of Nṛsiṃha.
I am your devotee, O best of the gods, and I ask you truly:
O Master, undivided devotion to you has arisen in me in many ways. / How have I become dear to you? Tell me the cause, O Lord.'
Nṛsiṃha said: / 'I shall tell you, O very wise one; listen with single-pointed mind / to the cause of your devotion, dear child, and why you are dear to me.
In a former time you were born to some twice-born man, but did not study; / your name was Vasudeva, and you were extremely attached to a prostitute.
In that birth you did not perform even a little good deed; / having consumed honey and clarified butter, you were solely eager for union with the prostitute.

"By the power of my vow, devotion has arisen in you, O sinless one."
Prahlāda said:
"Tell [me] in detail, O Lord of gods: what vow belongs to whose son?"
How was it somehow performed by me while dwelling with a prostitute? / Having shown mercy upon me, tell me everything now.'
Nṛsiṃha said: / 'Formerly Brahmā performed this incomparable [vow] for the purpose of creation; / by the power of my vow, the moving and unmoving world was created.
The vow was observed by Īśvara for the slaying of Tripura; / and by the power of this vow Tripura was cast down.
By many other gods, by ancient sages, / and by very wise kings this excellent vow was performed.
By the power of this vow, all attain perfection. / Those who became dear to me, having enjoyed numerous divine pleasures in heaven,

"Having enjoyed [it], they merged into me; but you, O Prahlāda, enter me,
since your avatāras are distinct from my body for the sake of [divine] work."
For them there is no return even in hundreds of great kalpas. / A poor man obtains wealth such as that of the giver of wealth [Kubera].
From it a desiring person obtains desire; one seeking a kingdom obtains an excellent kingdom; / one desiring long life obtains a lifespan like that of Śiva.
It brings non-widowhood to women, bestows sons and good fortune, / brings wealth and grain, and destroys sorrow.
Whether women or men observe this excellent vow, / to them I grant happiness, as well as the fruit of worldly enjoyment and liberation.
What is the use of speaking much, dear child, about the fruit of this vow? / Neither I nor Śaṅkara is capable of declaring the full fruit of my vow.'
Now I wish to hear the supreme rite of this vow: / in which month, O god, and on which day should it be, O Lord?
You ought to tell this in detail now, O god, / the rite by which indeed, O Master, one becomes a sharer in the complete fruit.'

Nṛsiṃha said:
"O child Prahlāda, may it be well with you; listen to the vow with a single-pointed mind:
one should perform it in the month of Vaiśākha, in the bright fortnight, on the fourteenth [day].
It is connected with my manifestation and is the cause of my satisfaction. / Listen, my son, to my appearance for the sake of the happiness of devotees.
In the western direction it took place, due to another cause. / This sacred place named Maulistāna is purifying and destroys sin.
In that sacred place there was a renowned brāhmaṇa, thoroughly versed in the Vedas, / named Hārīta, who was devoted to knowledge and meditation.
His wife was of great merit, constantly an embodiment of a virtuous wife, O lord, / named Līlāvatī, always devoted to her husband's control.
By the two of them great austerity was performed for a very long time, O son; / twenty-one yugas indeed passed there, without doubt. / Then in that sacred place I became visible to them.
Nṛsiṃha said: / 'Whatever you desire, O brāhmaṇa, that I grant without doubt.' / Then it was said by the two to him: 'If a boon is to be given to me,
then let a son like you be born to me right now!' / Then it was said by me, dear child: 'I am your son, without doubt.'
For I am Viśvakarman in person, the supreme Self, higher than the highest. / I will not reside in a womb, since I am indeed eternal.'
And then Hārīta said: “Let it be so, without a doubt.” / From then on, indeed, I have resided in that sacred field for the sake of devotees.
Coming here, the best of devotees should have [my] sight; / I constantly destroy all obstacles for him.
And for this reason, O best of men, those who perform this vow / in accordance with the proper rites have no fear.
Meditating on me in the form of a child, especially along with those two, / whoever performs the worship at night surely becomes Nārāyaṇa.
Having four arms, huge fangs, the form of Time, unapproachable, / resembling ten million suns, unapproachable as ten million Yamas, / having a face like a lion and limbs like a man,
one should always worship holy Nṛsiṃha, the divine lion, whose form is Time. / Having known this in particular, whoever goes to my abode,
[observes] this supreme, purifying, great vow that bestows an abundance of fortune, / and ultimately bestows liberation upon devotees, without a doubt.
When this vow of mine is performed, the fruit of a thousand Dvādaśīs [is gained], / especially on a Saturday conjoined with the Svātī constellation,
in conjunction with the Siddhi yoga, and likewise in the Vaṇija karaṇa. / A conjunction with all these yogas destroys ten million murders.
In conjunction with any one of these, my day destroys sins. / Knowing my day, whoever transgresses it is indeed an evildoer.
One who does not perform it goes to hell for as long as the moon and the sun [endure]. / When my day has arrived, my child, after first brushing the teeth,
my devotee, with senses subdued, [shall make] the solemn resolve for the vow before me: / “Today I shall perform your vow; bring it to completion without obstacle.”
One observing the vow must not engage in wicked conversation and the like. / Then, at noon, in the pure water of a river or similar place,
or at home, or in a temple tank, or in an auspicious pond, / the wise person should bathe with the Vedic mantra,
with clay, with cow dung, and with myrobalan fruit, / and with sesame seeds according to the rule, for the pacification of the flood of all sins.
Putting on two clean garments, he should undertake his daily rites. / Then, having smeared the house [with cow dung], he should make an auspicious eight-petaled [lotus].
Having set up a water pot there, made of copper and with a thread wrapped round it, / he should place upon it a vessel filled with grains of rice.
And there he should place a golden image of me together with Lakṣmī, / having fashioned it of gold according to his means, and then bathe it with the five nectars.
Then, having summoned a Brahmin preceptor who is not overly greedy / and who knows the sacred scriptures, placing him in front, he should worship the deity.
He should have a pavilion erected there, adorned with bunches of flowers. / I am to be worshipped according to rule with seasonal flowers,
with sixteen services, with mantras, and with restrictions. / Then he is to be worshipped especially with Purāṇic mantras:
sandalwood paste with camphor, mixed with thick saffron, / seasonal flowers, and tulasī leaves.
Whoever offers [these] to holy Nṛsiṃha is liberated; of this there is no doubt. / Incense made of black agallochum, always dear to Hari,

he should offer to Hari, the guru, for the attainment of all desired goals. / A great lamp should be presented, which destroys the darkness of ignorance, / and he should perform a great waving of lights accompanied by the ringing of bells.
“Food offering and sugar as well, accompanied by edible and chewable delicacies, / I offer to you, O lover of Ramā; bring about the destruction of all sins!”
The mantra for offering food: / “O Nṛsiṃha, O Acyuta, O Lord of gods, on your auspicious birthday, / I shall fast, renouncing all enjoyments.
Be pleased thereby, O Lord; remove the sins of this birth!” / A night vigil must be kept with the sounds of songs and musical instruments,
and the constant recitation of the Purāṇa centering on stories of holy Nṛsiṃha. / Then, at dawn, immediately after bathing,
he should worship me according to the aforementioned rite, making offerings to me. / With a tranquil mind, he should have a Vaiṣṇava ancestral rite performed before me.
Then the gifts that will be spoken of are to be given / to worthy, well-born recipients, out of a desire to conquer both worlds.
Together with that golden deity—which causes my satisfaction— / he gives cattle, land, sesame, gold, and the like to the twice-born.
A bed with a mattress should be given, accompanied by the seven grains, / and other things according to his ability, each given according to one's own means.
One desiring the stated reward should not practice deceit regarding wealth. / Afterward he should feed Brahmins and give them a generous sacrificial fee.

It must be done even by the poor; gifts should be given according to capacity. / All castes are indeed qualified for my vow; / but it should be performed especially by my devotees, those who are devoted to me.

Then the prayer mantra:
'Those men who have been born in my lineage, and those mortals who are yet to be,
deliver them, O Lord of gods, from the ocean of worldly existence that yields sorrow.'
For me, who am drowned in the ocean of sins and overwhelmed by aquatic creatures / in the form of diseases, and who have fallen into great distress,
grant me your hand of support, O Lord of the universe lying on Śeṣa! / Through this vow, O Lord of gods, become the bestower of enjoyment and liberation!”
Having prayed in this manner, then bidding farewell to the deity according to rule, / he should offer all the presents and other articles to the preceptor.
Having gratified the Brahmins with sacrificial fees, he should dismiss them. / Absorbed in meditation on me, he should eat together with his kinsmen.
Even a destitute person who regularly fasts on the fourteenth day / is released from sins committed over seven lifetimes; of this there is no doubt.
Whoever hears this sin-destroying vow with devotion, / by the mere hearing of it dispels the sin of slaying a Brahmin.
The person who proclaims this supreme, purifying secret / always attains all desires and the fruit of this vow.
Whoever performs this according to their ability at the time called midday, / [and] by the grace of holy Nṛsiṃha, the sage along with Līlāvatī,
worships with supreme devotion, attains eternal liberation. / Going to that sacred field, one who worships holy Nṛsiṃha
always obtains whatever is desired, by the grace of holy Nṛsiṃha. / O holy Nṛsiṃha of mighty form, unapproachable as ten million [gods of] Time,
fearful, destroying the distress of Hari, child-formed, praise be to you! / To holy Nṛsiṃha, the child, whose form is that of a boy,
all-pervading, delightful, whose nature is self-manifested, / the soul of all living beings, Lord of the universe, the self-luminous,
who abides within the solar orb, ocean of compassion, praise be to you! / To the one possessing twenty-four forms, whose form is the fire of Kalarudra,
whose unique form is the universe, to Nṛsiṃha praise be to you! / The god Nṛsiṃha, who conquered Vīrabhadra, holds on his forehead
the discs of the twelve suns, fiercely burning in full measure. / There is the highly meritorious Sindhu, a river especially delightful.
Near it, O beautiful one, there stands a city even today, / renowned as Maulistāna, ever fashioned by the gods.
There is the dwelling of the great-souled Hārīta; / and Līlāvatī stays right there, of this there is no doubt.
An echo occurs there near the Sindhu river. / When the Kali age arrived, sin-committing foreigners
dwelt right there in great numbers; of this there is no doubt. / Just as at the birth of Nṛsiṃha there was a supreme, wondrous roar,
When a man shouts loudly, 'Nṛsiṃha! Nṛsiṃha!', / such an echo indeed arises there, O daughter of the mountain.
Whether a killer of a Brahmin, a thief of gold, a drinker of liquor, or a violator of his teacher's bed, / those men who go to the Sindhu and especially bathe [there]
are liberated—of this there is no doubt—by the grace of the glorious Nṛsiṃha. / Indeed, those human beings who dwell [there] for the measure of ten nights
are to be known as doers of meritorious deeds; my word is not untrue. / Those castes, beginning with Brahmins, who dwell there in the Kali [age],
are to be recognized like Mlecchas, outside the Veda, by the foremost of the gods. / They eat meat there, and always drink liquor.
Therefore, they are embodiments of unrighteousness, most sinful, without a doubt. / Like Brahmins devoid of twilight worship, so too, outside the Veda,
they dwell in that town in the west, O ruler of gods. / There is only one supreme holy site, very extensive, named Nṛsiṃha, / hearing of which a man is immediately released from sin, without a doubt.
